articles.title: Why is the x86 undefined instruction called ud2? Why 2?
articles.summary: The x86 undefined instruction called ud2 is an architecturally undefined instruction that raises an invalid opcode exception when executed, guaranteeing a crash if the program attempts to reach it. This instruction is not named ud1 but is instead called ud2 due to its similar properties and the fact that it was the first to reliably raise an invalid opcode exception. The existence of ud2 is a result of the 0F FF and 0F B9 sequences, which were both found to cause invalid opcode exceptions, and the subsequent attempts to define a new instruction or modify the existing one.

articles.title: what if my git host were a static site generator?

This is a problem because static site generators like Forgejo are designed to handle a fixed number of requests per second, but the increasing number of GitHub users and the need to serve static HTML files can lead to scraper load. This can be mitigated by using a web application firewall like Anubis to block scrapers, but this goes against the philosophy of the open web by restricting access to the web app. A static site generator like Forgejo can be a better solution, as it can serve static files without the need for a web application firewall, and can be more resilient to scraper load.
